'''''Heliopsis helianthoides''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Asteraceae, known by the common names '''rough oxeye''',<ref name="BSBI 2007" /> '''smooth oxeye'''<ref name="PLANTS" /> and '''false sunflower'''.<ref name="USDA Plant Guide" /> It is [[native plant|native]] to eastern and central North America from [[Saskatchewan]] east to [[Newfoundland]] and south as far as [[Texas]], [[New Mexico]], and [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]].<ref name="FNA" /><ref name="mobot" /><ref name="BONAP" />

''Heliopsis helianthoides'' is a [[rhizomatous]] [[herbaceous]] [[perennial]] growing {{cvt|40|-|150|cm|0}} tall. The toothed leaf blades are oval to triangular or lance-shaped and may be smooth or hairy or rough in texture. The flowers are produced from midsummer to early autumn (fall).<ref name="RHS A-Z" /> The [[inflorescence]] contains one to many [[pseudanthium|composite flowerhead]]s. Each head contains yellow ray florets which are generally {{cvt|2|–|4|cm|frac=4}} long. The rays are fertile, having a small forked pistil at the base; this distinguishes them from [[Helianthus|true sunflowers]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Newcomb |first1=Lawrence |title=Newcomb's Wildflower Guide |date=1977 |publisher=Little, Brown & Company |page=390}}</ref> At the center are many yellow to brownish disc florets. The fruit is an [[achene]] about {{cvt|5|mm|2}} long.<ref name="FNA" />

In the wild, ''H. helianthoides'' may be found in wooded areas and [[tallgrass prairie]], and sometimes along roadsides.<ref name="USDA Plant Guide" />

It is a popular garden plant for moist, fertile soil in full sun. Plants grow stiff and tall, so may require staking. Several [[cultivar]]s are available with flowers of varying colors and shades. These include "Summer Sun", "Golden Plume", and "Prairie Sunset".<ref name="mobot" /> The "Benzinggold", "Goldgefieder", "Light of Loddon", and "Spitzentänzerin" [[cultivars]] of ''H. helianthoides'' [[variety (botany)|var.]] ''scabra'' ("rough")<ref name="RHS Latin for Gardeners" /> have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 43 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 3 March 2018}}</ref>

The Botanical Latin species name ''helianthoides'' means "resembling sunflowers".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book | last=Harrison |first=Lorraine | title=RHS Latin for Gardeners | year=2012 |publisher=Mitchell Beazley | location=United Kingdom | isbn=184533731X }}</ref>
[[File:PLC2780.jpg|thumb|False sunflower attracts a range of predatory arthropods including [[Jumping spider|jumping spiders]], which use the open flower heads as hunting platforms for visiting pollinators.{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}}|none]]
